title: Chess, But My Bishops Are Snipers
summary: Chess vs Stockfish where White's two bishops are Sniper Bishops: instead of moving, a sniper bishop may shoot (remove) an enemy piece on its diagonal line of sight while staying on its square. Each snipe costs the player's turn (changed from Midas Touch feedback). Narrator fianchettoes both snipers on the long diagonals, snipes developing pieces, and wins the main game; a secondary challenge to win using only the sniper bishops fails.
rules: Standard chess start; player White vs Stockfish (3600). Only White's two bishops are snipers.
Sniper bishop moves like a normal bishop, OR uses its turn to snipe: remove the first enemy piece on any of its diagonals (line of sight) without moving.
A snipe counts as the player's move for that turn.
Sniper bishops can be captured normally; trading them off removes the advantage.
Sniping the king is not allowed (checkmate required) [inferred].
